newsitem.title: USA: Florida commission advises execution by injection.
newsitem.headline: Florida commission advises execution by injection.

text.p: Florida corrections officials say the state should unplug its electric chair and use lethal injection to execute death row prisoners, a government spokeswoman said on Thursday.
Florida's controversial electric chair, known as "Old Sparky," has been at the centre of an ongoing controversy since flames shot from the head of a condemned killer during an execution in March.

Executions were halted until at least September and the state supreme court has ordered a new hearing to determine if the chair, which has malfunctioned twice in the past seven years, represents cruel and unusual punishment.

The Florida Corrections Commission voted last week to recommend the state dump the 74-year-old electric chair. Edie Ousley, spokeswoman for Gov. Lawton Chiles, said the governor's office had received the commission's report but had not yet had time to study it.

The commission recommended that Florida inmates already sentenced to die be given the choice between electrocution and lethal injection. Inmates sentenced after its passage into law would have no choice.
Advocates for lethal injection have failed to sway lawmakers at least three times in the past 10 years.

But the March 25 execution of Pedro Medina has focused more attention on Florida's method of execution. A 12-inch (30 cm) flame leaped from Medina's head and the execution chamber was filled with the smell of burning flesh.
Subsequent tests of the chair attributed the incident to human error.
Following Medina's fiery death, Florida attorney General Bob Butterworth urged a shift to lethal injection, the most common method of execution in the United States. Chiles has not taken a position.
The report was sent to the governor's office as well as legislative leaders. Only Florida lawmakers can change the method by which death row inmates are executed.
